content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices during bullish sentiment periods, especially after recent spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% when sentiment > 0.75 and price has recently risen.
- Overestimates prices in bearish sentiment windows; reduce forecast by 1–4% when sentiment < 0.33 and price has recently fallen.
- After a sharp price spike, model exhibits lagged overshoot — delay correction by 1–3 days and reduce slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Mean reversion is overestimated — if price deviates > 5% from 30-day moving average, apply corrective pullback of 0.5–1.5% per day toward mean.
- In high-event windows (≥20 events/30d), model overconfidently assumes continuity; reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.8% per event beyond 15.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to overpredict — apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias.
- For multi-event periods with policy_count > 0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per policy event to account for regulatory uncertainty.
